instructions.task: Does own ask the reader to answer a currently open question or settle a proposed choice?

criteria.true: The section requests an answer, including an implicit request that promotes a proposal to the owner for decision. A marked decision counts only when the surrounding text brings it to the reader for an answer.
criteria.false: It only reports a settled decision, explains a comparison, lists the author's assumptions or unknowns without bringing them for an answer, or asks only for comments. Explicit recorded acceptance later in full settles older open wording for that same choice.

reference.boundary: Judge the section's own text, read with its parent opening. A proposal is not acceptance, but an explicitly labelled proposal alone is not a request for a reader answer. Do not infer a new request from a historical quotation. Feedback alone can use Comments. full supplies the enclosing section including its children, so recorded answers there can settle an older request in own.

yes.finding: This section asks for an answer without a native choice in its section; inspect the request and the matching guide's answer component.

instructions.task: Does control ask its reader to settle a currently open design choice described in context?

criteria.true: At least one answer settles or authorizes a currently unsettled choice about domain, storage, architecture, contracts, product behavior, design structure or a consequential design correction. Confirmation is included when its yes authorizes the proposed design. A multi-answer control is included when any answer settles or authorizes such a design change; that does not make its other procedural answers design decisions.
criteria.false: Every answer is only comprehension or feedback that settles and authorizes no design change, a hypothetical example, or a choice already settled by an explicit source-recorded owner decision. A local saved response or initially selected option alone is not source-recorded owner acceptance.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, does the text state what design choice the reader is deciding?

criteria.true: The preceding text identifies the concrete choice, in ordinary prose or a heading.
criteria.false: Only the control names the choice, or the preceding text never identifies it.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, is the current model drawn?

criteria.true: A preceding figure, flow, sequence, state, topology or other drawn view shows what exists today.
criteria.false: Only prose or a table describes today, or any drawing occurs only after this control.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, are the concrete alternatives drawn as changes to the current model?

criteria.true: Each alternative has a drawn change to the picture, including an explicit unchanged-picture option.
criteria.false: At least one alternative has no drawn change; a prose label or comparison table alone is not a picture.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, does the comparison say what each alternative gains?

criteria.true: The preceding comparison explains a concrete benefit of each alternative.
criteria.false: A benefit is absent for at least one alternative or appears only in or after the control.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, does the comparison say what each alternative costs?

criteria.true: The preceding comparison explains a concrete cost of each alternative.
criteria.false: A cost is absent for at least one alternative or appears only in or after the control.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, does the comparison identify who bears each alternative's cost?

criteria.true: Each cost's bearer is stated or unambiguously identified by the preceding explanation.
criteria.false: The reader must guess who pays at least one cost.

instructions.task: Before the occurrence of control in context, does the author recommend one alternative?

criteria.true: The preceding text explicitly recommends one alternative.
criteria.false: There is no explicit preceding recommendation; an initially selected answer alone is not a recommendation.

reference.status_boundary: control identifies one native answer control through its id and title. context holds complete enclosing heading sections in source order and may repeat nested text. For applicability, read the identified control and all relevant source status, including an explicit source-recorded owner decision after the control. Recorded acceptance settles older open wording for that same choice. Distinguish source-recorded acceptance from a local saved response, a recommendation and initial selection. A confirmation that authorizes a design change is a decision request even when phrased as checking understanding. A multiple-answer control is in scope if any answer settles or authorizes a design change, without reclassifying all its procedural answers.
reference.brief_boundary: For the seven briefing properties only, judge the portion of context BEFORE the occurrence of this identified control, ignoring its option summaries and everything after it. Identify the occurrence by control id/title, not a different question. Drawings may be Mermaid, native flow/board/trace, SVG or figures, but the supplied representation must preserve the evidence needed for that proposition. Text describing a picture is not a drawing. If supplied context cannot settle a proposition, return an in-between assessment rather than inventing missing context.

no.finding: The text before this control does not identify the decision; read the enclosing brief before presenting it.
The text before this control does not show the current model drawn; inspect the enclosing brief.
The comparison before this control does not draw every option's change; inspect the enclosing brief.
The comparison before this control leaves an option's gain unstated.
The comparison before this control leaves an option's cost unstated.
The comparison before this control does not identify every cost's bearer.
No explicit recommendation appears before this control; inspect the enclosing brief.
